title: ERM++: An Improved Baseline for Domain Generalization
note: Variant: uniform running mean of all weights from step 2k to 20k under the PF cosine schedule (weight_avg mode uniform, start 2000) plus BN recal, a free extra readout from the same PF runs once arm 2 code exists. Gate: ema_9998_bn or swad_bn passes its screen, so averaging is worth widening. Other ERM++ parts: warm start is PF already; longer schedule is the parked 30k item; train+val retrain belongs to the final model, not a screen.

title: Foreground Sampling and Spatial Support in Pavement Crack Segmentation
note: Not covered by any arm: decoder normalisation (GroupNorm for the decoder BatchNorm2d, encoder keeps BN) was never varied here, with batch 8 of five mixed sources; rcs oversamples whole cells so it does not touch crop reachability or norm layers. Needs a small norm-swap code path. Evidence is from scratch U-Net on Crack500, so card should fix a fold-0 pre-screen first. Card can add the frozen-encoder-BN variant from P309.

title: Surgical Fine-Tuning Improves Adaptation to Distribution Shifts
note: Not covered by any arm: permanent per-block freezing (stem+layer1-2 tuned with layer3-4 held at ImageNet, and the reverse) is a hard depth split chosen by shift type, while PF only freezes 1k steps and SPD decides per tensor by gradient sign. Config-level via PF group lr_mult if per-block groups are supported. E1 is an input-level shift (scuff, contrast), the case the paper says favours early layers. Absorbs P353 (freeze layer4).

title: Rethinking the Hyperparameters for Fine-tuning
note: Cost: a 3 x 2 x 2 grid is 12 configs at about 11 GPU-h each on CV, and the lr question is already partly asked by the encoder_spd fold-0 control (lr_mult 1.0) against PF (0.1). Evidence is classification only. Reopen after encoder_spd and modern_recipe read out, using their winning lr_mult as the grid centre.

title: LiNeS: Post-training Layer Scaling Prevents Forgetting and Enhances Model Merging
note: Variant of the WiSE encoder readout: alpha rises linearly with depth (stem near ImageNet, layer4 near PF) instead of one constant alpha, plus the inverse ordering since our erasure is in layer3/4; BN recal on the training fold, alpha cross-fitted. Inference only. Gate: P1 and P2 loss-barrier pre-checks pass and the constant-alpha WiSE readout shows any F51 inactive or crack gain.

title: Neural Network Optimization Reimagined: Decoupled Techniques for Scratch and Fine-Tuning (DualOpt)
note: encoder_spd tests the same mechanism (pull encoder weights back toward the pretrained anchor inside the optimizer, per layer adaptive); L2-SP is already the named fallback. No code found, abstract only, no numbers. Reopen only if SPD passes and a stronger anchor method is wanted.

title: Sharpness-Aware Gradient Matching for Domain Generalization (SAGM)
note: The arm sam is parked in WAVE2_REVIEW (weak prior, 2x cost); SAGM is a replacement for SAM and the scout itself says run only if SAM moves E1. Evidence is classification only. Reopen with sam if soft_band_jml or swad_const passes.

title: Progressive growing of patch size: Curriculum learning for accelerated and improved medical image segmentation
note: Weaker evidence than P044 for a sampling and crop change (3D medical, +1.28% relative Dice, no code found for this version). It needs a new crop sampler and variable batch size, and inactive and edge_dark need whole-cell context, so the benefit is doubtful. Crop curriculum is untested here (BRIEF 5 only has 2x resolution), so not VOID; reopen after rcs and P044 read out.

title: Fast Trainable Projection for Robust Fine-Tuning (FTP)
note: encoder_spd tests the same projection-toward-pretrained family, and in the SPD paper segmentation table SPD beats FTP in distribution (74.27 vs 73.79 per the ledger and scout records). Learned radii add a hyper-optimisation loop on 478 cells. Reopen as a comparator only if SPD passes.

title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution (LP-FT)
note: PF is already a short LP-FT (1k frozen steps, then 0.1x encoder lr) and won E1 inactive (BRIEF 5, optimizer row), and the encoder_spd fold-0 control covers the opposite end (no damping). Only the length of the LP phase (about 5k steps) is untested; reopen as a PF freeze-length variant if encoder_spd fails its mechanism gate.

title: Rethinking "Batch" in BatchNorm
note: Precise-BN recalibration on the training fold is already built into ema_wise_posthoc (bn_recal, raw_bn row). The remaining variant, encoder BN frozen at ImageNet stats, has only review-level evidence with no numbers; it can be added as a second arm inside the P044 normalisation card if that is opened.

title: DGSAM: Domain Generalization via Individual Sharpness-Aware Minimization
note: The arm sam is parked (weak prior, 2x cost) and DGSAM is a SAM variant. Preprint with no code found, abstract-level evidence, classification benchmarks. The per-source perturbation idea would need source-balanced batches that break pairing. Reopen only if sam is reopened.

title: Training Beyond Convergence: Grokking nnU-Net for Glioma Segmentation in Sub-Saharan MRI
note: T1 spec already lists schedule length (PF at 30k, 5 folds x 1 seed, about 8 GPU-h) as a parked item after the stack. The 80k to 160k steps asked here cost 4x to 8x per run (about 45 to 90 GPU-h per 5 fold seed), and the evidence is secondary summaries not checked in full text. Reopen with 30k first, ERM++ P003 also asks for longer training.

title: Revisiting Fine-Tuning Strategies for Self-supervised Medical Imaging Analysis
note: The question (permanent freeze of the deepest block, layer4 at ImageNet) is a sub-case of the P166 surgical arm, which has stronger evidence (ICLR, shift-type analysis). Run it inside the P166 card as one block split if that is opened. Its own evidence is for self-supervised medical encoders.

title: Why is SAM Robust to Label Noise?
note: Mechanism note for the parked sam arm, not a new recipe. Its useful parts are covered more cheaply: earlier-checkpoint readouts come from EMA and SWAD in ema_wise_posthoc and swad_const, and label-jitter robustness is tested by soft_band_jml. Reopen only if sam is reopened and the explicit Jacobian regulariser is wanted at 1x cost.

title: Focal-SAM: Focal Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Long-Tailed Classification
note: Depends on plain sam, which is parked, and the scout says run only if SAM helps. Classification only, abstract-level evidence, no code found. Long-tail pixel losses are a different family (T2 or long-tail loss arms); rcs already tests the data-side tail effect.
